quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle. Use high beams only on rural roads when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.
When pulling next to or away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when pulling next to a curb and when leaving a curb.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood may affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol can harm your judgment and coordination. This can make it unsafe to drive, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your thinking and reflexes. It makes it hard to react quickly while driving.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
Other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more time and space to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down.

questions.question: When passing another car, you have enough space to return to the driving lane:

options.text: If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, you can return to your lane safely when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: While driving at night, a vehicle coming toward you has its high beams on. You should:

options.text: Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates that:

options.text: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
Passing is not permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are together, only the side with the broken line can pass.

questions.question: A driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass the vehicle slowly at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and only move when all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use which lights to see better?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include biological sex, how much food is in their stomach, and how many drinks they have had. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no traffic from either direction can cross to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop faster than cars. Following too closely endangers both you and the motorcyclist. You need space and time to avoid a crash if they stop suddenly.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turns are not allowed here.
You can turn left only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turns are not allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is prohibited. This sign prohibits left turns.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
After you pass the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you have enough space from the vehicle you passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed the same.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not speed up or brake. Keep the same speed and let the other vehicle safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events:

options.text: Causes traffic jams.
Prevents rear-end crashes.
Improves traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic jams.
questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events. This "rubbernecking" causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: What does "implied consent" mean?

options.text: You must take a chemical test if asked to check your blood alcohol level (BAC).
You must take a field sobriety test to show if you are impaired.
You must have a physical exam before you get a license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must take a chemical test if asked to check your blood alcohol level (BAC).
questions.explanation: Any driver on a Maryland road agrees to take a test for alcohol or drugs in their blood. The MVA will suspend your license if you take the test and have a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into the right lane when you can see the headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: In a vehicle on a highway, is it legal to drink alcohol?

options.text: No. You cannot drink from or carry open alcohol containers.
Yes, if you are not the driver.
Yes, if you are driving but not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. You cannot drink from or carry open alcohol containers.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol. Drivers and passengers cannot have open alcohol containers in a vehicle while it is running.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and know no trains are coming.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up so you don't cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.
